comment: What a kind of site changes about the ORDER of a report, never about a number. A kind moves the findings it leads with up one severity level (never to critical) and the ones it defers down one; the usual order then applies. Blocking findings are never listed and never moved. The same judgements are written out for the model in skills/audit/sections/site-kind.md - keep the two in step.

docs.label: a documentation or reference site
docs.note: A reference page is read one section at a time and an engine lifts one section, so answer-first writing and structure count for more here, and machine-readable authorship for less.

spec.label: a specification or standard
spec.note: Authority comes from the document being the standard rather than from a byline, so structure, stated evidence and schema coverage count for more here, and machine-readable authorship for less.

publisher.label: a publisher or blog
publisher.note: An engine choosing between two accounts of the same event picks the one it can date and attribute, so authorship and freshness count for more here.

saas.label: a SaaS or marketing site
saas.note: Marketing prose is where unsupported claims and paragraphs that only make sense in sequence concentrate, and the brand has to resolve to an entity, so self-contained passages, stated evidence and organisation markup count for more here.

ecommerce.label: an ecommerce catalogue
ecommerce.note: Product and offer markup is what gets a catalogue into an answer at all, so schema coverage and valid markup count for more here.

local.label: a local business
local.note: A local business has to resolve to one place with one name and one address, so organisation markup and consistent brand details count for more here.
